$comment: Desi Maximalism type direction. Fonts come from foundations/typography/source/pairings.json plus the newPairings below (all Google Fonts, SIL Open Font License, credits checked against Google Fonts METADATA.pb files and the designers' pages; see research.md 2.3 and 7). Sizes are rules of thumb unless a source is given.
character: Painted-signboard confidence: heavy or high-contrast display letters, often with a flat drop line, set big inside a framed cartouche. Latin and Indic scripts sit side by side as equals, each in a face designed for it. The body face is plain and very readable, because the surface around it is not.

anatomy.$comment: What to look for when judging a typeface for this approach.

weight.want: Heavy (700-900) or a high-contrast display cut
weight.why: Must hold its own against dense pattern; sign painters and matchbox labels used bold, filled letters.

contrast.why: Echoes hand-painted cinema and shop lettering and 19th-century poster faces (Rozha One's Latin is drawn from them).

scripts.want: Latin plus Devanagari (and other Indic scripts where the audience needs them), designed together
scripts.why: Matched x-heights and weights let bilingual headlines sit as one block; system fallbacks break the rhythm.

conjuncts.why: Hindi, Marathi and Nepali text needs them to be correct; missing conjuncts are errors, not style.

counters.why: Survive outlines, drop lines and small sizes on busy grounds.

body.want: Humanist or mono-linear sans with an Indic companion
body.why: Calm reading inside a loud piece.

avoid: 'Indian-style' Latin fonts that fake a headline bar or Devanagari strokes
Handwriting fonts for headlines or body (the hand lives in the painting; one Kalam note is allowed)
Any font without the conjuncts the text needs

fit.$comment: core = recommended, good = works, accent = special cases, avoid = not for this approach. None of the shared pairings supports an Indic script, so the core choices are the newPairings.

bricolage-figtree.why: Bricolage's heavy, slightly quirky display weights stand up to pattern; Latin-only, so pair with Mukta or Baloo 2 for Indic text.

young-onest.why: A heavy, soft serif that reads like painted sign lettering; Latin-only.

fraunces-commissioner.why: Fraunces at 800 has the bounce and weight of shop-sign lettering; keep WONK off; Latin-only.

instrument.why: Condensed high-contrast serif suits fashion and editorial maximalism, but its single regular weight is light against dense pattern.

alegreya.why: Calligraphic and literary; for storytelling pieces with a quieter border.

nunito.why: Rounded and friendly for kids' or community work; looks soft next to heavy borders.

source.why: Very readable for long text on pages in this style; too calm for display.

schibsted.why: Built for maximum restraint; disappears against ornament.

plex.why: Engineered and technical; at odds with festive, painted surfaces.

rozha-mukta.why: Signboard didone display with a matching Devanagari, over Ek Type's humanist Mukta. The default.

yatra-baloo.why: Railway-sign brush lettering over a rounded, warm body; the most hand-painted feel.

poppins-mukta.why: Geometric heavy weights for matchbox-label and modern pop pieces; Latin and Devanagari in nine weights.

newPairings.name: Bazaar Signboard
newPairings.mood: Bold, high-contrast display letters like a hand-painted cinema hoarding or shop sign, with a calm humanist body. Latin and Devanagari designed to sit together.
newPairings.bestFor: Posters, packaging, food, fashion and cultural events in this style; bilingual Latin and Hindi or Marathi headlines.

display.designer: Indian Type Foundry (Devanagari: Tim Donaldson and Jyotish Sonowal; Latin: Shiva Nallaperumal)
display.notes: Single weight that is already heavy. Latin recalls 19th-century poster lettering. Very tall x-height; use at large sizes on screen. On Google Fonts since 2014.

body.designer: Ek Type (Girish Dalvi and Yashodeep Gholap)
body.notes: Seven static weights (200-800). Sister families: Mukta Vaani (Gujarati), Mukta Mahee (Gurmukhi), Mukta Malar (Tamil).

newPairings.name: Painted Railway Sign
newPairings.mood: Brush-cut display letters from Mumbai's hand-painted railway signs over a rounded, friendly body. Warm, local, a little playful.
newPairings.bestFor: Street food, cafés, community events, kids and family brands, social posts.

display.notes: Inspired by hand-painted Mumbai railway signs; the Latin borrows the Devanagari brush angle. Single weight. On Google Fonts since 2016.

body.notes: Variable weight. Sister families cover nine Indic scripts plus Arabic (Baloo Bhai 2, Baloo Paaji 2, Baloo Thambi 2, etc.).

newPairings.name: Matchbox Geometric
newPairings.mood: Heavy geometric letters like a modern matchbox or sticker label, with a humanist body for reading.
newPairings.bestFor: Apps, launches, fashion and music in a pop-maximal register; labels and stickers.

display.designer: Indian Type Foundry (Latin: Jonny Pinhorn; Devanagari: Ninad Kale)
display.notes: Nine static weights with italics. One of the first Devanagari typefaces with a full range of weights. On Google Fonts since 2015.

body.designer: Ek Type (Girish Dalvi and Yashodeep Gholap)

scripts.$comment: Mixing Latin and Indic scripts. Rules of thumb.
scripts.matching: Match the visual size of the scripts, not the point size: Devanagari usually needs the same or a slightly larger size to look equal to the Latin x-height. Align on the Latin baseline; the Devanagari headline bar (shirorekha) should sit near the Latin x-height.
scripts.leading: Devanagari needs more room for vowel signs above and below: add 10-20% leading over Latin-only settings.
scripts.order: The audience's main language first and larger; the second script below, at the subhead size.
scripts.otherScripts: Use a family with a matching sister for the audience's script: Mukta (Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Tamil), Baloo 2 (nine Indic scripts plus Arabic). For long Hindi text, Tiro Devanagari Hindi (Tiro Typeworks: John Hudson and Fiona Ross, with Paul Hanslow) is a literary serif option. For Urdu, choose a Nastaliq face with a fluent reader.
checks: Every Indic line is written or reviewed by a fluent reader; never machine-translated.
Never use Indic letters as texture or pattern.
Test the conjuncts actually used, at the actual size.

handwritten.$comment: Handwritten accent faces from foundations/typography/source/handwritten.json. use: none | accent (one short element) | core (part of the style). A product picks one in brand.json -> typography.hand.
handwritten.why: The hand lives in the painted lettering; one pen note in Kalam (Devanagari and Latin designed together) can add the shopkeeper's voice.

typeWithArt.weightMatch: Headline stems at least as thick as the frame's major outline (about 1.25% of the short side), so the type holds against the border.
typeWithArt.dropLine: Optional signboard drop line: a flat copy of the headline in ink, offset down-right by about 3% of the font size. Flat, never blurred. Not on body text.
typeWithArt.scaleMatch: Headline block width 60-85% of the cartouche's inner width; the medallion stays larger than the headline block.
typeWithArt.alignment: Centre the headline inside a symmetrical cartouche; left-align body text and anything longer than 3 lines.
typeWithArt.spacing: Headline at least one band width from the cartouche frame; pattern stops 2% of the short side outside the cartouche.

sizes.$comment: Headline cap height as a share of the canvas height, and body text minimums. Rules of thumb. Slightly larger than humanist-minimal, because the type competes with pattern.
sizes.viewingDistance: Sign-industry rule of thumb: about 1 inch (25 mm) of letter height for every 10 feet (3 m) of viewing distance for basic legibility; double it for comfortable reading, and more on patterned grounds.

measure.source: Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (45-75), narrowed slightly for busy pages (rule of thumb)

setting.case: Sentence case for headlines and body. Short labels and brand plates may be spaced capitals (1-3 words).
setting.rag: Centred headlines balanced line by line (text-wrap: balance); body ragged right; no justified text.
setting.numbers: Prices and dates in the body face's bold (Mukta or Baloo 2 also carry Devanagari numerals); the mono only for codes.

rules: Bold or high-contrast display type in a framed, pattern-free cartouche.
Latin and Indic scripts from families designed together; Indic text checked by a fluent reader.
Three sizes and two weights per piece; sentence case.
A flat drop line is the only lettering effect; no outlines-only, bevels or shadows.
No fake 'Indian' Latin fonts and no script as texture.
At most one pen note in Kalam (six words or fewer); never the headline, body or numbers.
